analysis.title: High Yield & Loan Strategy: Looking out the Private Credit window
key_insights: BofA expects private credit (PC) to start a recovery cycle in 2027 through new deals rather than legacy portfolios. Better deal flow, higher compensation and better terms are the mitigants. Software concentration, a smaller revenue footprint and rising interest costs keep weighing on older vintages and on blended returns.

North American PC fundraising reached $105bn through 3Q26, up 21% from $87bn a year earlier. The rebound rests almost entirely on a record 2Q26 of $72bn (including $46bn in direct lending), against $15bn in 2Q25. 3Q26 fell back to $15bn, and the number of funds closed diverged sharply from the amount raised, so the recovery's durability is in question.

PC distributions have recovered consistently while private equity (PE) distributions have not, and PC net distributions turned positive in 2024. Since distributions correlate with future fundraising, they may be a more durable support than the single record quarter.

LTM PC gross issuance is $111bn as of 3Q26, down 25% YoY from $148bn. BofA's forward indicators point to $118bn over the NTM, a 6% rise, still well below the 2024 peak. Fundraising has historically led deployment by 2-3 quarters, so the record 2Q haul should support 2027 underwriting.

The issuance recovery is expected in new money rather than refinancings. Refinancing volume is migrating from direct lenders into the broadly syndicated loan (BSL) market, even though BDC portfolios face large near-term maturity walls.

PC new-issue spreads have widened about 20bp YTD to roughly 520bp. BofA expects another 20bp over the NTM to 540bp, a gradual normalization rather than a sharp repricing. Elevated rate volatility is the main driver, partly offset by lower leverage on recent deals.

BofA projects the NTM BDC non-accrual rate at 3.6% in its base case, up from 3.4% using current marks (2.9% as of Q2). Loans marked below 80 have a 20-50% chance of entering non-accrual within 12 months, against under 1% for loans marked above 95. Mapped through the KBRA relationship (two-quarter lead), this gives a 7.0% PC default rate for 2027, versus 8.9% in a COVID-style shock scenario.

BDC stress is framed as an equity problem, not a credit problem. Aggregate PC leverage is below 1x, and unlisted BDCs hold only $350bn of the asset class, with about $190bn of equity (roughly 15% of PC). Redemptions at the 5% per quarter limit are expected to continue, leading to selective downgrades rather than collective distress.

The PC spread premium over BSL fell to about 210bp in 3Q26 from 246bp in 2Q26, and stayed near 180bp against B2/B3 loans. BofA sees room for further compression as BSL takes refinancing from PC borrowers and narrows the quality gap, even as absolute PC spreads edge wider.

Relative value favors PC over PE. Rate hikes and geopolitical shocks stalled the expected PE recovery, 2022-vintage software and services equity stakes are likely underwater from AI disintermediation, and higher debt service takes cash flow from equity. Absent a jump in earnings, capital is expected to reroute to senior debt.

PC secondaries reached $20bn in 1H26, up 122% from $9bn in 1H25 and already equal to FY2025. GP-led deals were $17bn against $3bn LP-led. Turnover rose to 1.5% in 1H26 from 1% in 2025, and BofA forecasts $40bn of volume in 2027 at 2% turnover. If PC AUM reaches $3tn by 2030, volume could reach $120bn a year.

AI-related USD credit issuance totals $572bn YTD: $259bn in IG, $43bn in HY, $16bn in institutional loans and $252bn in private credit, direct lending and bilateral. IG AI spreads tightened to 139bp from YTD wides of 150bp, a 63bp premium to ex-AI. HY AI spreads tightened 69bp WTD to 376bp from a record 445bp, a 180bp premium to ex-AI (196bp), inside last week's 227bp wide.

HY spreads tightened 13bp WoW to 314bp as rates volatility fell to an intra-month low, for a +0.75% weekly total return (MTD +65bp). BBs and Bs tightened 14bp while CCC spreads were flat. IG is ahead of HY MTD at +175bp, and loans trail HY by over 95bp.

HY technicals: funds took in $1.2bn after a flat week and two weeks of outflows. Primary was light at $2.7bn priced WTD, with 43% for acquisition financing and a below-average 45% for refinancing. Internal demand was $3.5bn this week and $4.0bn next week.

The week saw net HY upgrades of $859mn after four weeks of net downgrades. PBF Holding ($801mn) was the largest upgrade and Cogent the largest downgrade ($468mn). United Rentals became a rising star with $8.4bn of indexed debt. Rising stars total $59.0bn YTD against $37.0bn of fallen angels.

HY defaults total $16.8bn YTD with 37 cent average recovery, and loan defaults total $24.4bn with 54 cent recovery. October added one distressed exchange and one hard default in HY, and the same in BSL. The LTM loan default rate is 1.8% by par and 2.3% by issuer.

USD loans returned +0.34% WTD, led by CCCs at +0.93%, with the index price at 94.5. YTD loans are +2.99%, BBs +4.07% and CCCs -8.97%. Demand exceeded net supply by $1.2bn WTD, and YTD demand net of supply is about +$92.5bn against +$79.1bn a year ago.
The BofA HY Credit Stress Indicator (CSI) is 38.2%, down 2.4% WoW on better credit access and lower HY volatility. The Loan CSI is 58.1%, up 2.1% on higher loan volatility.

Large loan price drops came from Balrog Acquisition (-13.7pts, Moody's negative outlook) and INEOS US Petrochem (about -11pts after weaker Ineos Quattro Q3 EBITDA of €162mn against €177mn). In EUR loans, Kronosnet CX Bidco fell 13pts after Bloomberg reported a skipped interest payment.

market_movers.rationale: United Rentals was upgraded to BBB3 and became the latest HY rising star with $8.4bn of indexed debt. This is a credit rating action tracked by BofA, not an equity call.
CoreWeave is on BofA's HY downgrade-candidate list ($7.8bn face, 908bp OAS, B1). Its unsecured bond trades 5.75 points of yield above its loan, and its HY bond price rose 2.6 over the week.
Charter's CCO Holdings debt is a downgrade candidate (BB3, $82.5bn face, 297bp OAS). It also screens 334bp rich to its CSI-implied OAS, and CCO Holdings is on the fallen-angel watchlist.
Oracle appears on the fallen-angel watchlist (BBB2, $119.5bn face, 236bp OAS). Its 2026 AI-related bond issues priced 95-195bp over Treasuries.
FMC is on the HY downgrade-candidate list (BB1, 1,109bp OAS, $3.95bn face) and screens cheap to its CSI-implied OAS by 304bp.

sector_views.rationale: BofA favors PC over PE. Higher debt-service costs and underwater equity in software and services weigh on PE, while PC distributions have recovered and capital is expected to reroute to senior debt.
Redemption pressure at the 5% per quarter limit is expected to persist through 2027. BofA treats it as an equity problem with only selective credit downgrades.
High software and services concentration, plus AI disintermediation risk for 2022-vintage deals, keeps older PC vintages vulnerable to non-accruals and defaults.
Media had the largest 4-week downgrade volume, driven by the Skydance (Paramount) downgrade. Cable was the weakest HY sector in October at -260bp.

earnings_insights: Ineos Quattro reported weaker Q3 EBITDA of €162mn against €177mn in the same quarter last year, as pricing gains from Iran war-related import disruptions fade (reported, per BofA loan commentary).

Moody's revised the outlook on Balrog Acquisition to negative, citing sales declines in 1H26 and elevated leverage expected over the next 12-18 months, amid consumer budget pressure and rising input costs.

trade_ideas.description: Relative value: favor private credit over private equity
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher debt-service costs and underwater equity stakes in challenged sectors should drive PE underperformance absent a significant earnings rebound.
trade_ideas.risk: A significant jump in PE portfolio earnings would remove the case for PC outperformance.

trade_ideas.description: Rich/cheap screens: cheap names in overweight segments (SABHLD, IEP, ARGID, FMC) against rich names in underweight segments (CHTR, GTN, IONPLA, GT)
trade_ideas.rationale: Issuers trading wide or tight to their issuer-level CSI-implied OAS. The cheap basket averages 681bp against 446bp implied.
trade_ideas.risk: BofA states the screen is indicative only and not a recommended list.

risk_factors: Refinancing pressure and software/services exposure keep older PC vintages vulnerable to rising non-accruals and defaults.
The 2026 fundraising rebound is concentrated in one quarter and fell back to $15bn in 3Q26.
Elevated rate volatility is the primary driver of wider PC spreads and of uncertainty in new-deal pricing.
Large near-term maturity walls across BDC portfolios raise refinancing risk.
AI disintermediation could put 2022-vintage software and services equity underwater, and remediation needs capital infusions BofA does not see broadly.
Persistent unlisted BDC redemptions at the 5% per quarter limit.
CCC credit remains weak (CCC HY -5.3% YTD, CCC loans -8.97% YTD).
AI-related credit carries a spread premium over ex-AI (180bp in HY, 63bp in IG) and hit record wides last week.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 and 2: North American private credit capital raised by quarter, with 2Q26 at a record $72bn and 3Q26 at $15bn, per Preqin.
Exhibit 10: Share of performing BDC exposure entering non-accrual within 12 months by starting-price bucket, with loans marked below 80 at 20-50% and loans above 95 under 1%.
Exhibit 11: Table of NTM non-accrual rates by fair-value bucket. Base case is 3.6% non-accrual and a 7.0% default rate, against 3.4% / 6.7% at current marks and 5.2% / 8.9% in a COVID-style shock.
Exhibit 14: PC spread premium to the overall BSL market fell to roughly 210bp in 3Q26 from 246bp, and stayed near 180bp against B2/B3 loans.
Exhibit 18 and 20: IG AI-related spreads at 139bp against ex-AI 76bp, and HY AI-related spreads at 376bp against ex-AI 196bp, with AI premiums of 63bp and 180bp.
vol_and_positioning: Rates volatility fell to an intra-month low this week. The HY CSI inputs show HY volatility down 16.3% WoW and rates volatility down 8.4%, while the Loan CSI shows loan volatility up 14.7%.
HY funds returned to $1.2bn of inflows after a flat week and two weeks of outflows. MTD flows are neutral, with $1.6bn of fund outflows offset by $1.7bn of ETF inflows.
CCC HY spreads were flat WoW at 1,307bp, with CCC performance lagging the rally (MTD CCC return -1.96%). Decile 10 issuers trail the HY index by 5.52% MTD and 14.7% YTD.
HY bid-ask spreads are elevated at 0.33pt against 0.32pt a week ago. Telecoms and Capital Goods led trading volume at about 1.5x their 3-month average.
Unlisted BDC redemption pressure persists at the 5% of AUM per quarter cap, which BofA treats as an equity problem for the vehicles.
geopolitical: BofA says geopolitical shocks and rate hikes reversed its early-2026 expectation of a friendlier rate environment and open exit markets for private equity.
Ineos Quattro's weaker Q3 results are linked to fading pricing gains from Iran war-related import disruptions.

tension_points.bull_case: Better vintages with higher spreads and tighter terms, fundraising up 21% YTD, improving distributions and a 2-3 quarter fundraising lead on deployment support a 6% rise in issuance in 2027. An AI-related sentiment hit could push issuers toward PC for capex funding.
tension_points.bear_case: Legacy portfolios stay stressed, with non-accruals rising to 3.6% and a 7.0% default rate. Fundraising was concentrated in one record quarter and fell to $15bn in 3Q26, and refinancings are migrating to BSL.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fundraising stays near the $15bn 3Q26 level instead of recovering, since BofA notes it leads deployment by 2-3 quarters. Non-accruals rising toward the 5.2% COVID-style shock case would also weaken the thesis.

tension_points.bull_case: Aggregate PC leverage is below 1x, unlisted BDCs are only $350bn of the asset class, and redemptions affect a contained cross-section at 5% per quarter, so credit impact is limited to selective downgrades.
tension_points.bear_case: Redemption pressure persists through 2027 at the highest allowable rate, BDC portfolios face large near-term maturity walls, and low-marked loans have a 20-50% non-accrual rate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Aggregate PC leverage rising above 1x, or non-accruals rising well beyond the base case, would turn an equity problem into a credit problem.

theme_stances.key_argument: Better deal terms, improved fundraising and distributions should feed a PC recovery cycle in 2027 even as legacy portfolios stay challenged.
theme_stances.evidence: we think that emerging mitigating factors will feed a recovery cycle in PC in 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher debt-service costs and underwater equity stakes should drive PE underperformance, with capital rerouted to senior debt.
BDC stress is mainly an equity problem because aggregate PC leverage is below 1x and unlisted BDCs are a small share of the asset class.
theme_stances.evidence: All told, BDC credit problems amount to selective downgrades, not collective distress.
